'''Platform 8127/121''' was an [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Golan III Space Defense NovaGun]] [[Space station/Legends|space station]] that [[Orbit/Legends|orbited]] the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Esseles/Legends|Esseles]] in [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]]. Measuring 2,600 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in length, it had a considerable armament composed of [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolaser]] batteries, [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedo]] launchers, and [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beam]] projectors. It was present when [[Imperial Advisor/Legends|Imperial Advisor]] [[Coh Veshiv]] [[Capture of Coh Veshiv|transferred]] from his personal [[Corvette/Legends|corvette]], the ''[[Empire Forever]]'', to the seemingly Imperial [[Frigate/Legends|frigate]] ''[[Far Orbit]]''. However, the ''Far Orbit'' was actually a disguised [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] [[Privateer/Legends|privateering]] vessel, and its crew kidnapped Veshiv.

==Description==
Platform 8127/121 was a [[Golan III Space Defense NovaGun]], an armed [[Space station/Legends|space station]] of the [[Golan space defense platform]] line produced by [[Golan Arms/Legends|Golan Arms]]. Measuring 2,600 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in length, it had a sizable armament of [[Turret/Legends|turrets]]&mdash;fifty [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolaser]] batteries, twenty-four [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedo]] launchers, and fifteen [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beam]] projectors. Each tractor beam and turbolaser had a crew of three, while the proton torpedo launchers had crews of two.<ref name="Orbit" />

While at full capacity, a total of 880 crew members and 228 [[Gunner/Legends|gunners]] staffed Platform 8127/121. At a skeleton crew, the space station could still operate with 220 hands, while its weapons could be staffed by fifteen gunners. Platform 8127/121 possessed at least one [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|deflector shield generator]] and also had [[Sensor/Legends|sensor]] arrays. Capable of carrying 15,000 [[Metric ton/Legends|metric tons]] of cargo and up to three [[Standard month/Legends|months]] worth of [[Foodstuff/Legends|consumables]], the Golan III also had room to carry a hundred [[Trooper/Legends|troopers]].<ref name="Orbit" />

==History==
By [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]],<ref name="Date">{{FarOrbitDate}}</ref> during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] between the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], Platform 8127/121 [[Orbit/Legends|orbited]] the Imperial-controlled [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Esseles/Legends|Esseles]],<ref name="Orbit" /> which was located in the [[Essesia system]] in the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]]' [[Darpa sector/Legends|Darpa sector]],<ref name="CCW" /> which also fell in the [[Arrowhead]] region of [[The Slice/Legends|the Slice]].<ref name="Atlas" /> In 0 ABY, the [[Imperial Advisor/Legends|Imperial Advisor]] [[Coh Veshiv]] visited Esseles on a fact-finding tour in his [[CR90 corvette/Legends|CR90 corvette]], the ''[[Empire Forever]]''. Following their arrival there, the CR90 stayed near jump point 180:45:115, which was in the sights and range of the Golan III's weapons. Shortly after Veshiv arrived at Esseles, the seemingly Imperial [[EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate/Legends|EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate]] ''[[Far Orbit]]'' turned up as well and requested an orbit of the world parallel to the ''Empire Forever''{{'s}} orbit; however, the frigate was actually a disguised Alliance [[Privateer/Legends|privateering]] vessel, whose crew intended to [[Capture of Coh Veshiv|capture Veshiv]]. Upon convincing the ''Empire Forever''{{'s}} [[Captain/Legends|captain]], [[Annance]], that the ''Far Orbit'' would take up the role of Veshiv's [[Transport/Legends|transport]] for the rest of his journey, Captain [[Dhas Fenoep Vedij]] of the EF76 arranged for the [[Advisor/Legends|advisor]] to be transferred to his [[Starship/Legends|ship]].<ref name="Orbit" />

{{RPGseed}}
Vehsiv was taken to the ''Far Orbit'' in his personal [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]], the ''[[Myrenia]]''. Once the advisor and his shuttle were aboard the Nebulon-B, the ''Far Orbit'' jumped to [[Lightspeed/Legends|lightspeed]], and its privateer crew succeeded in capturing Veshiv. Because the frigate was in [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]], the Imperials in the shuttle could not contact the ''Empire Forever'' or Platform 8127/121 for assistance. Veshiv was then handed over to the Alliance for a cash reward.<ref name="Orbit" />
{{Endgame}}

==Behind the scenes==
Platform 8127/121 first appeared in the [[roleplaying game]] adventure ''[[The Capture of Coh Veshiv]]'', from [[1998]]'s ''[[The Far Orbit Project]]'' by [[Timothy S. O'Brien]]. ''The Far Orbit Project'' was a supplement to [[West End Games]]'s ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' and was a sequel of sorts to the previous publication, ''[[Pirates & Privateers]]'', carrying on that book's theme by following the privateer vessel ''Far Orbit''. If the privateers reveal themselves as they attempt to capture Veshiv when he is on the ''Far Orbit'' but before the frigate jumps to hyperspace, it is possible for the ''Myrenia''{{'s}} crew to alert the ''Empire Forever'' and Platform 8127/121 to what is happening. If this is the case, the ''Far Orbit'' must jump away while being fired upon by the pair.<ref name="Orbit" />
